findings.finding: The plan's mechanism for preserving dbca AC3 — mapping a bare WorkflowError 'execute-step outage wrapper (current contract uses the `execute step failed:` message form)' to llm_unavailable while other bare WorkflowError go to command_failed — is keyed to a production wrapper that does not exist. The string 'execute step failed' appears NOWHERE in src/rebar; it exists only as a synthetic fixture constructed inside tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py:101 and test_workflow_error_codes_35ab.py:77. The only production site that raises a bare WorkflowError in the whole workflow package is editor.py:475 (the missing-bundle case the plan routes to command_failed). Genuine execute-step LLM outages propagate as LLMUnavailableError (gate_dispatch.py preflight()/mid-run), which the retained branch already maps to llm_unavailable. Distinguishing the two bare-WorkflowError cases therefore requires message-prefix sniffing — an anti-pattern the codebase explicitly forbids for error routing (see LLMBudgetExhaustedError / RunawayToolLoopError docstrings: routing 'must never sniff messages') — to protect a case with no production source.
